correctness.rationale: Using the canonical F_1=F_2=1 encoding with a_1=0 and infinite zero padding, parsing zero followed by one as D and other zeros as S is unique and records only complete-block boundaries. The admissible word counts satisfy w_0=w_1=1 and w_m=w_{m-1}+w_{m-2}. An independently written exact checker enumerated the complete prime interval and additionally generated the admissible word sets to test equality, not only the sizes. It reproduced all twenty counts, thresholds and last words. In particular 135,340 primes through 1,803,947 fill exactly 10,946 length-20 classes; DSSDSSSSDSDSSSSS first occurs at that prime. The maximum of the exact first-hit primes proves coverage at the stated bound and failure at all lower bounds. Chang–Verwee Theorems 1.5–1.6 also justify existence for general fixed lengths in this convention.
residual_risks: Exact exhaustion is for the stated twenty lengths. No numerical conclusion is drawn for larger lengths, and no formal proof-assistant check was performed.
